speaker: alse_pinder
text: Do not trip on the bag, sir. There is a man in your chamber. Mistress sent him. I am only the door, and the door is telling you before the stair does.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Come up. I had the joiner's man in because the stool has rocked since Christmas, and I am tired of a chair that argues with a man who is trying to write. He is paid when I say he is paid. You are not the purse.

speaker: (the joiner's man)
text: Short leg, mistress. It has been standing on a fold of paper. I have the fold out. The stool will stand on the wood now, if the floor is the floor and not a boat.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: A fold of paper. Let me see it before it becomes a story. Three leaves, by the thickness. Foul paper. Cut, not fair.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Three leaves of something you cut. I can see ink. I cannot see a price. Are discarded words valuable, Master Shakespeare? I ask because I have been housing them under a piece of furniture, unpaid, since the year turned.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Not where they were. Under a leg they were a wedge. On a desk they were a comedy I cut in January. Value is a place, Mistress. They have changed places.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: They're the only words in this room that ever held anything up. You may bow to that or you may argue with a level stool. I know which I prefer.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: It does not rock. I put a hand on it. Anne's cushion is still on the seat. The cushion is not what was holding the short leg. The paper was. The cushion can go back to being a cushion.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The cushion stays. She made it. The paper comes out, and it does not go into the fire tonight out of embarrassment. I cut those leaves. I can own them in my hand as easily as I owned them under a leg.

speaker: (the joiner's man)
text: Threepence was the figure the mistress named at the door. I have done the leg. I have not done a lecture. If the paper is a relic, that is between the poet and the stool.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Threepence, and here it is, from my purse, because I ordered the work. You will not pay me back out of a share you have not got this hour, and you will not write it into a letter as if Stratford had mended your furniture.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not pay you back, and I will not send the stool to Anne. The threepence is yours to have spent. The leaves are mine. January's cut. Not a speech I am going to read to the kitchen to prove they were once clever.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Were they Latin? I only ask because Latin is what the floor shouts on a Monday, and I cannot tell a clever cut from a cross word when both are ink.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They were not a schoolroom. They were a comedy with too much of itself. I am not going to tell you which scene. A scene that could not hold a play has held a stool, and Mistress has said the better sentence already.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: I have, and I do not need it improved. The stool is level. The cushion is Anne's. The man has his threepence. You have your dirty papers. Put them on the shelf if you mean to keep them, and do not put them back under the leg to feel thrifty.

speaker: (the joiner's man)
text: Level. I will take the threepence and the bag, and I will not tell the next house I propped a poet on his own leavings. Good night, mistress.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Good night. Mind the third stair. It sounds like a drum if you trust it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: On the shelf, then. In the hand first. The ink is on the paper and on the finger, which is the ordinary state of the finger. I am keeping the wedge. It is a private measure, and it is not a joke I am telling at supper.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Supper is done without you, and threepence of board was not asked because you were not at the board. Do not invent a meal to forgive me a joiner. I am not sorry. The rocking offended me more than your poetry did, and your poetry was not asked.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Not asked, and not valuable where it was. Valuable here only as a thing that kept a short leg honest. I can live with that rating. It is sterner than Garnish, and cheaper.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Cheaper than a new leg. I am glad of that. A new leg would have been a story, and this is only paper, and paper I can dust.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Dust round it, not at it. Master Shakespeare, your carrier-day face came up the stair ahead of you. I am not asking what the letter said. If the house in Stratford is well enough to write, the house in Great St Helen's can stand level. That is all the moral I have, and I have spent it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The house there has written. The cough is gone. That is the only piece of it I am spending on this landing. The rest of the sheet is not a stool's business. The wedge is on the shelf when my hand has finished looking at it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will leave the light. If you stand in the chamber smiling at three dirty leaves, I shall assume the stool has converted you, and I shall not come in.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Come away, Alse. Threepence paid. One poet left with his leavings. A level chair. I call that a Thursday well mended, which is more than I say of most Thursdays.
